scenes.title: Proof, Style and Arrangement
scenes.summary: Three things concern a speech: the sources of its proofs, its style, and the arrangement of its parts. The proofs and the sources of enthymemes have been treated; style comes next, for it is not enough to have what one should say, one must also say it as one should.

scenes.title: Delivery
scenes.summary: In the order of nature the facts came first, then their setting out in style, then delivery, which has the greatest power but has never been treated: it came late into tragedy and rhapsody, and concerns the volume, pitch and rhythm of the voice. Actors now count for more than poets, and delivery wins in politics too, because of the depravity of the hearers; it is thought vulgar, but it is necessary.

scenes.title: Style in All Teaching
scenes.summary: Style makes some small difference in all teaching, though no one teaches geometry this way. Skill in delivery is a gift of nature, style a matter of art, so prizes go to those who master it, and written speeches owe more to their style than to their thought.

scenes.title: The Poets and Prose
scenes.summary: The poets first set style in motion, since words are imitations and the voice is our most imitative part. Because they won fame with simple thoughts, the first prose style was poetic, like Gorgias'; but prose and poetry have different styles, as the tragedians show by turning to the iambic and giving up words outside ordinary speech. Only the style of prose is treated here; the other belongs to the books on poetics.
